title: Gaming monitor deals UK: best Black Friday screens from £63.99 to OLED

- **Best overall:** AOC Agon Pro AG276QZD2AM 27-inch OLED, £289.99
- **Best cheap:** Samsung Odyssey G5 32-inch, £159
- **Best under £100:** Dell SE2726HG 27-inch 240Hz, £89.25
- **Best ultrawide:** Philips Evnia 34M2C5691QA, £219.99
- **Best splurge:** LG UltraGear OLED 45GX900A, £979

All prices were reported on 27 November 2026 in TechRadar's Black Friday gaming monitor roundup. Black Friday prices usually last until Cyber Monday (30 November). For more, see [every Black Friday 2026 guide](/black-friday/).

body:
## How to choose a gaming monitor

Four things matter more than the brand name. Get these right for the machine you play on and you'll be happy with almost any of the screens above.

- **Resolution:** 1080p is fine on a 24-inch screen and easy for budget PCs to run fast. **1440p is the sweet spot** for 27 to 32 inches and most mid-range graphics cards. 4K looks sharpest, but you need a powerful PC (or a console) to drive it, and most PCs won't hit high frame rates at 4K.
- **Refresh rate:** 144Hz is the minimum we'd call a gaming monitor. 240Hz and above helps in fast shooters if your PC can produce that many frames per second. If it can't, you're paying for speed you never see.
- **Panel type:** IPS gives good colours and viewing angles. VA has deeper blacks but can smear slightly in dark, fast scenes. **OLED** has perfect blacks and near-instant response; it costs more, and you should let it run its built-in care routines to avoid screen burn.
- **Connections:** for a PS5 or Xbox Series X, look for **HDMI 2.1** so you can play at 120Hz. PCs should use DisplayPort where they can.

## Which screen suits which player

**First gaming PC or a teenager's bedroom:** the Philips Evnia 24-inch at £63.99 or the Dell SE2726HG at £89.25. The Dell's 240Hz is the better buy if the PC is fast enough; otherwise the Philips is plenty. If you're also buying the computer, see our [laptop deals guide](/guides/laptop-deals-uk/).

**Mid-range PC:** the Samsung Odyssey G5 32-inch at £159 is the one we'd buy for most people. 1440p at 165Hz on a big curved screen is a noticeable upgrade from a 24-inch 1080p monitor, and £159 is a low price for this size.

**Console players:** the Lenovo LOQ 27Q-10 at £129 (Argos) has two HDMI 2.1 ports, so a PS5 and a PC can stay plugged in at once. The AOC U32G4U at £268.99 gives you 4K for console games and a 1080p 320Hz mode for competitive PC shooters. Our [PS5 Black Friday guide](/guides/ps5-black-friday-deals-2026/) has controller and headset deals to go with it.

**Sim racing, flight sims and multitasking:** an ultrawide. The Philips Evnia 34-inch at £219.99 is the value pick; the MSI MPG 346CQRF X24 at £248.98 adds 240Hz.

**The best picture:** OLED. The AOC Agon Pro 27-inch at £289.99 is a low price for a 1440p OLED this fast, and it's our overall pick. The LG UltraGear 45-inch at £979 is a showpiece, but its discount is small.

## Good prices to look for

As a rough guide from this week's deals: a 24-inch 1080p 144Hz screen for under £70, a 27-inch 240Hz for under £100, a 32-inch 1440p for under £170, a 34-inch ultrawide for under £250 and a 27-inch 1440p OLED for under £300 are all good prices. Monitor prices often dip again in the January sales and around Amazon's Prime Day events in the summer, but Black Friday is usually one of the cheapest points of the year.

Prime members get free fast delivery on most Amazon monitors. If you're not a member, a [Prime free trial](https://www.amazon.co.uk/amazonprime) covers the sale and you can cancel before it ends.

Buying for someone? Our [gifts for gamers guide](/guides/gifts-for-gamers-uk/) has ideas under £20, £50 and £100.

## FAQs

### Is 1080p or 1440p better for gaming?

For screens of 27 inches or more, 1440p. Text and games look noticeably sharper, and most mid-range PCs can still run it at well over 100 frames per second. 1080p is fine on a 24-inch screen or with a budget PC.

### Do I need a 240Hz monitor?

Only if your PC regularly goes above about 144 frames per second, which is common in esports games like Valorant, Counter-Strike 2 and Fortnite on lower settings. For slower single-player games, 144Hz to 165Hz is plenty.

### Is an OLED gaming monitor worth it?

If you can stretch to around £300, yes for most gamers. Blacks are perfect and motion is extremely clear. The trade-offs are lower full-screen brightness than some LCDs and a small risk of burn-in if a static image stays on screen for very long periods.

### Which gaming monitor is best for PS5?

Look for HDMI 2.1, which lets the PS5 run at 120Hz. The Lenovo LOQ 27Q-10 has two HDMI 2.1 ports. A 4K screen like the AOC U32G4U makes the most of the PS5's 4K output.

### When is the best time to buy a gaming monitor in the UK?

Black Friday to Cyber Monday is usually the cheapest time of year, with the January sales and Prime Day in the summer close behind. If a monitor you want is near the prices above, there's little point waiting.
